extracted.intended_audience: self-publishing authors, independent authors, and anyone seeking to hire book editors
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide to current book-editing rates by service type and to evaluating/finding professional editors; includes hourly/word/page ranges and selection checks. Intended to help authors budget and choose appropriate editorial services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of your manuscript plays a significant role in determining editing rates. Longer manuscripts often require more time and effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer manuscripts increase overall cost because they require more editor time; consider manuscript length when budgeting and requesting quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Different editing levels, such as developmental editing, line editing and proofreading, come with varying degrees of complexity. Rates adjust accordingly, reflecting the depth of scrutiny and refinement needed for your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which level(s) you need (developmental, line, copyediting, proofreading, etc.) because each has different hourly/word/page rates and affects total cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond basic editing, additional services like formatting, fact-checking or indexing contribute to the overall cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing quotes, clarify which services are included (e.g., formatting, fact-checking, indexing) because add-on services raise the price; be explicit in contracts about scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor's experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The expertise and experience of the editor also influence rates. More seasoned editors may command higher fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher fees often correspond to greater proficiency and a more polished final product; weigh experience against budget and request portfolio evidence or references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Urgency can impact book editing rates. Quicker turnaround times often incur higher costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead where possible to avoid rush fees; ask potential editors for realistic turnaround estimates when requesting quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing requirements can vary across genres. Technical or specialised subject matter may demand a more in-depth editing process, thus affecting the overall cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect higher rates for technical, medical, legal, or heavily-researched non-fiction; confirm the editor's genre experience when evaluating suitability and price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding industry benchmarks for book editing rates is vital. By being aware of the prevailing standards, you can make informed decisions and avoid potential exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published ranges (e.g., Editorial Freelancers Association) as a sanity check when comparing offers; beware unusually low rates that may signal low quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghostwriting (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ghostwriting involves a collaborative process where a skilled writer enhances or crafts a manuscript on your behalf, capturing your voice and vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA suggested hourly ghostwriting rates between $75 and $126; per-word and per-hour examples by genre are given (e.g., fiction 25¢–50¢/word; business 50¢–$1/word; hourly $80–$125 depending on type). Ghostwriting can reduce later editing needs but is a high-cost service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental editing (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Developmental editing focuses on refining the manuscript’s structure, content and coherence; the editor collaborates to enhance narrative, characters, and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA industry rates typically range $55–$95 per hour; per-word and pages-per-hour tables by genre are provided (e.g., fiction 3¢–5¢/word; pages/hour 5.5–10). Consider how much developmental work your manuscript needs vs. budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line editing (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Line editing addresses sentence structure, language use and overall readability, adding polish to prose and elevating engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA guideline range $47.50–$85.00 per hour; per-word and pages-per-hour tables by genre included (e.g., fiction 2.7¢–3.5¢/word; pages/hour 5.0–9.5). Line editing is time-consuming and priced accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyediting (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyediting focuses on grammar, spelling, punctuation and consistency throughout your writing, transforming prose by infusing precision and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA recommended range $45–$75 per hour; tables show per-word and pages/hour ranges by genre (e.g., fiction 2.7¢–3.5¢/word). Confirm the level of copyedit (light vs. heavy) when requesting quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading is the ultimate checkpoint before publication, eliminating typos, errors and formatting inconsistencies as the conclusive editorial step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA recommends $35–$75 per hour; per-word and pages/hour tables by genre are provided. Use proofreading as final verification after prior editing stages; it is less intensive than copyediting or line editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checking involves thoroughly verifying information within your manuscript against reliable sources to enhance credibility and rectify inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA rates hover between $55 and $60 per hour and an example pages-per-hour metric (25 pages/hour) is given. This service is essential for non-fiction where accuracy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing (definition & rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing systematically organises keywords and topics to make the text a reader-friendly reference, enhancing usability and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFA-recommended indexing rates typically range $50–$60 per hour; example per-word (11¢) and pages-per-hour (6–8) metrics are provided. Indexing is a specialized, add-on service often priced separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated cost for a 50,000-word book
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated total costs for a 50,000-word book vary widely by service: the post offers approximate ranges from $600 to $75,000 depending on the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example table (EFA-based) shows: Ghostwriting $12,500–$75,000; Developmental $1,400–$3,400; Line editing $1,350–$3,000; Copyediting $1,000–$2,750; Proofreading $600–$2,250; Indexing $5,500. Use these as rough guides and get precise quotes for your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify the editor's accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by verifying the editor’s accreditation and affiliations with professional organisations related to editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check memberships (e.g., Chartered Institute of Editing and Proofreading; Editorial Freelancers Association; ACES; Council of Science Editors; Editors Canada; others listed). Accreditation suggests ongoing training and adherence to a code of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the editor's portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the editor’s portfolio to confirm their experience with your genre; a specialised portfolio indicates expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for verifiable links to books edited, publishers' pages, or marketplace listings. Platforms such as Reedsy or Upwork can be sources but verify quality and relevance to your genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request a sample edit, price quote and turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: Request a sample edit from the editor to gain insight into their skills and approach, and ask for a detailed price quote and estimated turnaround time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sample edit helps assess compatibility; get written estimates that specify scope, deliverables, and timelines so you can compare candidates fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read testimonials and verify references
rubrics_metrics.description: Review testimonials from previous clients to gauge the editor’s work quality, paying attention to testimonials with verifiable contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, contact references or look for independent verification of claims to ensure transparency and reliable feedback before hiring.
